the development of a new pulsed eddy current (PEC) inspection system for monitoring and detecting degradation in nuclear steam generators, including the support structures.
the development of new methods for non-destructive evaluation and monitoring of support structure integrity in nuclear steam generators.
the development of new methods for the inspection and monitoring of SG support structures.

pulsed eddy current combined PCA has been demonstrated to be a viable method for inspection of steam generator tubes in the presence of support structures.

pulsed eddy current inspection combined with PCA is a promising technique for assessing support structure degradation and fouling, and for detecting and sizing frets at supports.
pulsed eddy current combined PCA can be used to inspect tubes and support structures simultaneously and can provide information on relative position of the tubes within the SS410 support structure.

The main takeaway from our work is that
pulsed eddy current combined PCA is a promising technology for monitoring support structures in SG tubes.
pulsed eddy current combined PCA can be used to measure gaps between tubes and supports, and to size frets at the tube/support interface, in either the absence or presence of fouling.
